Molecular-to-Megastructure Simulation Bridge. Connects atomistic material models with component, machine, building, and infrastructure simulations.

This database covers the technology as item 211 entry 74 of Manon's "100 Ultra-Advanced Future Technologies" catalog, section "Simulated Worlds and Reality-Scale Models". It is the public edition: every factual claim below is drawn from real public science and engineering, honestly labeled.

Feasibility tier: experimentally supported. Multiscale modeling is standard practice (QM to continuum); a general bridge across all scales is unproven.

Classification: public database. This record profiles the technology; companion records cover known science, constraints, approaches, tools, unresolved problems, evidence, and outlook.

title: Molecular-to-Megastructure Simulation Bridge - Known Science Foundations
description: Public edition: Connects atomistic material models with component, machine, building, and infrastructure simulations.
body:
Known science foundations of Molecular-to-Megastructure Simulation Bridge.

Density functional theory feeds molecular dynamics; MD feeds finite elements; FE feeds structural models. The Materials Project links scales for materials. True general bridging — arbitrary molecule to megastructure in one validated chain — needs scale-bridging methods (quasi-continuum, HMM) that remain research-grade.

Key quantity check (Length scales bridged in orders of magnitude / scales in a full bridge): computed ratio 0.6 against the reference value, relative error 0, within the stated tolerance of 0.3. This calculation was executed in Node.js at build time and the output stored verbatim.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

title: Molecular-to-Megastructure Simulation Bridge - Physical and Engineering Constraints
description: Public edition: Connects atomistic material models with component, machine, building, and infrastructure simulations.
body:
Physical and engineering constraints on Molecular-to-Megastructure Simulation Bridge.

Each scale transition loses information. Rare events at small scales control large-scale failure. Validated chains exist only for narrow material classes.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 0.72 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is bridged orders vs validation cases at 0.72 orders of magnitude (validation cases larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.

Unresolved problems for Molecular-to-Megastructure Simulation Bridge, in priority order (research burden index 22, 2 blocking):

Validated end-to-end chains (severity 3/3, tractability 2/3, BLOCKING; priority 9).

Rare-event capture (severity 3/3, tractability 2/3, BLOCKING; priority 9).

Generalizing beyond narrow materials (severity 2/3, tractability 2/3; priority 4).

These are open problems, stated plainly. A technology with unresolved blocking problems is not ready, whatever its promise.
